title: de Jong alteration diagram for a geometrically irreducible generic fibre
statement:
Let $S$ and $W$ be integral excellent Noetherian schemes of finite dimension, and let $g:W\to S$ be proper and dominant. Write $\eta$ for the generic point of $S$ and assume that $W_\eta=W\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ is geometrically irreducible of dimension $d\geq1$. There are integral excellent Noetherian schemes $S_1,P_1,\ldots,P_d$ of finite dimension, an alteration $b:S_1\to S$, a tower $P_d\xrightarrow{q_d}P_{d-1}\to\cdots\to P_1\xrightarrow{q_1}P_0=S_1$, and an alteration $h:P_d\to W$ such that $g\circ h=b\circ q_1\circ\cdots\circ q_d$. Each $q_j$ is proper, flat and of finite presentation; every geometric fibre is a nonempty connected reduced curve of pure dimension $1$ with at worst ordinary double points. Here an ordinary double point means that its completed local ring on the geometric fibre is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. No surjectivity of $P_d\to W\times_SS_1$ on the vertical components is asserted.

An alteration is a proper surjective morphism finite over a dense open of its integral target. Properness, flatness and finite presentation use [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Integrality, excellence, geometric irreducibility, fibres and dimension use [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]; finite morphisms and geometric fibres use [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and [def-weil-geometric-fibre].

source.place: Theorem 5.9 (i)--(iii), Situation 5.8, printed pp. 615--617, with trivial input group and empty boundary; forget the group, sections and projective structure. Local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online.

proof.text: Prove the assertion by strong induction on $d\geq1$, uniformly for all the bases in the statement. If $d=1$, apply [lem-trf-excellent-base-marked-semistable-curve] to $W\to S$ with $Z=\varnothing$. Its square gives $S_1$, $P_1$, $b$, $h$ and the single curve map, with all the required fibre clauses. The finite-dimension verification for its excellent Noetherian sources is included in Step 11 below. Hence assume $d\geq2$ and the assertion for all positive dimensions less than $d$.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, first two sentences; Theorem 2.4 for the dimension-one base case

proof.text: Put $K=\kappa(\eta_S)$. The integral finite-type scheme $W_K$ has one irreducible component. By [lem-pur-finite-inseparable-geometric-reduction] choose a finite purely inseparable extension $K'/K$ for which $(W_{K'})_{\mathrm{red}}$ is geometrically reduced. Normalize $S$ in $K'$ using [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension], obtaining integral $S_0$ with function field $K'$. This normalization is finite: for every affine domain $A$ of $S$, excellence implies Nagata by [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata]; the prime $0$ in [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] says exactly that the integral closure of $A$ in $K'$ is a finite $A$-module. The finite dominant map $S_0\to S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and its closed image contains the generic point, hence is all of $S$.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, purely inseparable normalization of S; Stacks 04KT, 035H, 032R, 032F

proof.text: Geometric irreducibility of $W_K$ makes $W_{K'}$ irreducible. In $W\times_S S_0$ take the reduced closure $W_0$ of its generic fibre, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The generic fibre of $W_0\to S_0$ is $(W_{K'})_{\mathrm{red}}$ by [lem-pur-reduction-generic-fibre]; it is geometrically integral: after every further field extension, the reduction immersion still has nilpotent defining ideal (the rings are Noetherian), hence the same underlying irreducible space as the corresponding base change of $W_K$, and Step 2 supplies geometric reducedness. The map $W_0\to W$ is finite: affine locally the base change of the finite algebra of $S_0$ is a finite module and its quotient is still finite. It is dominant (its generic fibre contains the point over the generic point of $W$), hence surjective because it is finite and therefore closed. It is an alteration. The morphism $W_0\to S_0$ is proper by base change and closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. The finite dominant generic-fibre map to $W_K$ and [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension] give generic dimension $d$. The schemes $S_0,W_0$ are integral excellent Noetherian of finite dimension by Step 11.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, geometrically reduced preparation; Stacks 054Z, 01J3, 02JX

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometrically-integral-curve-factorization] to $W_0\to S_0$. Write its proper birational modification as $X\to W_0$ and its factorization as $X\xrightarrow{v}Y\to S_0$. Thus the generic fibre of $v$ is a geometrically integral curve, and that of $Y\to S_0$ is geometrically integral of dimension $r=d-1\geq1$. All these schemes are integral excellent Noetherian and of finite dimension. The modification is surjective because its closed image contains a dense open. It is finite over that open, so it is an alteration.

Apply [lem-trf-excellent-base-marked-semistable-curve] to $v:X\to Y$, with empty boundary. Denote its square by $C\to X$ over $B\to Y$ and its curve map by $c:C\to B$. Both horizontal maps are alterations, $C$ and $B$ are integral excellent Noetherian, and $c$ is proper flat finitely presented with the required geometric curve fibres and smooth geometrically integral generic fibre. The composite $B\to S_0$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] and dominant. Its generic fibre is integral of dimension $r$: $k(B)/k(Y)$ is finite because $B\to Y$ is an alteration, and [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] computes both dimensions over $K'$. No geometric irreducibility of this generic fibre is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, Theorem 2.4; the group-free argument retains only the curve family

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-generic-components-split] to $B_{K'}$, giving a finite separable extension $L/K'$ over which all components are geometrically irreducible. Normalize $S_0$ in $L$, obtaining a finite surjective integral alteration $S_2\to S_0$ by the construction of Step 2. Choose a component of $B_L$ dominating $B_{K'}$ and take its reduced closure $B_2$ in $B\times_{S_0}S_2$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Such a component exists: a prime of the nonzero finite-dimensional $k(B)$-algebra $k(B)\otimes_{K'}L$ gives its generic point. There is no smaller prime after localization since this algebra is zero-dimensional, so its closure is a component of $B_L$. Consequently $B_2\to B$ is finite dominant (as in Step 3), hence an alteration. Its generic fibre over $S_2$ is the chosen reduced component [lem-pur-reduction-generic-fibre], geometrically irreducible by the splitting node, and has dimension $r$ by [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension] on its finite dominant map to $B_{K'}$. Properness of $B_2\to S_2$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Step 11 supplies excellence, Noetherianness and finite dimensions.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, preparation before induction; in the absence of group constraints use finite generic-component splitting instead of Lemma 5.5

proof.text: The induction hypothesis now applies to $B_2\to S_2$: its generic dimension is $r=d-1$, not $d$, and all its other hypotheses were checked in Step 6. Obtain an alteration $S_1\to S_2$, a tower $Q_{d-1}\to\cdots\to Q_0=S_1$ of $d-1$ required curves, and an alteration $Q=Q_{d-1}\to B_2$, commuting over $S_2$. The composite $Q\to B$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], and surjective because both factors are surjective. It is finite over a dense open: if $U\subset B$ makes $B_2|_U\to U$ finite and $V\subset B_2$ makes $Q|_V\to V$ finite, remove from $U$ the closed image of $B_2|_U\setminus V$. That image omits the generic point because $B_2$ is integral and finite dominant over $B$, whose generic fibre is its single generic point. On the remaining dense open both maps are finite, and products of their finite module generators prove their composite finite. Thus $Q\to B$ is an alteration.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, induction on relative dimension and composition of alterations

proof.text: Set $P=C\times_B Q$, with its two projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map $q_d:P\to Q$ is proper flat and finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. For any geometric point of $Q$, its fibre is exactly the fibre of $c$ at the composite geometric point of $B$, by the fibre-product universal property. Hence it is nonempty connected reduced of pure dimension one, with only the stated ordinary double points. In particular the last curve can be appended without any claim about vertical components of $W\times_S S_1$.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, final fibre product; Stacks 01W4, 01U9, 01TS

proof.text: The scheme $P$ is integral. Indeed, $Q\to B$ is dominant, so $P_{k(Q)}$ is obtained by extending the ground field of the smooth geometrically integral generic fibre of $c$; it is therefore integral and nonempty by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Q$ and a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}D\subset P$ above it, flatness and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] make $D$ flat over the domain $A$. Tensoring the injection $A\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}A$ gives an injection $D\hookrightarrow D\otimes_A\operatorname{Frac}A$, by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The latter ring is the ring of a nonempty affine open of the integral generic fibre: it cannot be zero by injectivity. It is a domain, hence so is $D$. Thus $P$ is reduced and every nonempty open meets its integral generic fibre. Two nonempty opens then intersect there, so $P$ is irreducible as well. This establishes integrality without selecting or normalizing a component, which could destroy flatness of the curve map.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, verification of the final fibre product; elementary affine flatness argument

proof.text: The projection $P\to C$ is proper and surjective by base change of the alteration $Q\to B$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence, lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Over the inverse image in $C$ of the dense open of $B$ where $Q\to B$ is finite it is finite: affine locally tensoring its finite module generators gives finite generators after base change [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. This inverse image is dense and nonempty since $C$ is integral and dominates $B$. Hence $P\to C$ is an alteration. Composing it with $C\to X\to W_0\to W$ gives an alteration $h:P\to W$; composing $S_1\to S_2\to S_0\to S$ gives an alteration $b:S_1\to S$. For either composite the same dense-open removal argument of Step 7 applies successively; properness is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Put $P_j=Q_j$ for $j<d$ and $P_d=P$. The defining squares and the fibre-product projections give $gh=bq_1\cdots q_d$ exactly.

source.place: Theorem 5.9 proof, final commutative diagram and alteration verifications

proof.text: All auxiliary schemes formed by finite morphisms, proper modifications, reduced closed subschemes of finite-type schemes, or the final curve base change are of finite type over one of the original excellent Noetherian schemes or an induction output. Thus they are excellent by the affine finite-type statement [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Finite total dimensions follow from [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension]: a finite dominant map or proper birational modification has relative function-field transcendence degree zero, and the proper dominant maps $C\to B$ and $P\to Q$ have transcendence degree one. In the base case this proves $\dim B=\dim S$ and $\dim C=\dim B+1<\infty$; in the induction step $B$ is an alteration of finite-dimensional $Y$, $S_2$ is finite over $S_0$, $B_2$ finite over $B$, and $P$ has dimension $\dim Q+1$. The intermediate $Q_j$ already have finite dimension by induction. This also justifies every earlier application requiring finite dimension. All required clauses now hold.
